merge_note: Four scouts returned. Orchestrator screened OUT as recent-repeat or over-worn (data center cooling/gas/energy, broadband, rural telehealth, satellite/sensor defense, myAlaska agentic): Begich 'energy-rich/stranded gas', Berkowitz 'global hub in four years', Schuerch 'Port MacKenzie 10-20GW', Stan Jones 'power costs too much', Mahoney 'North Slope inevitable' (also UNCONFIRMED verbatim), Mahoney '100 GW by 2030', Begich 'connectivity prerequisite/Starlink', Boufard/Ted Stevens 'AI for Arctic domain awareness' (overlaps 06-15 satellite/sensor correction). The viable, fresh-terrain candidates below are passed for the six-point gate.
claims_already_corrected_last_6_issues: 06-15: 'satellites don't work up here' / Arctic sensor gap is integration latency not satellite absence (DEFENSE)
06-14: Alaska 30deg cooler than Texas / $150M/yr PUE cooling savings (DATA CENTER COOLING)
06-13: broadband buildout done, all Alaskans access tech careers from home (BROADBAND/WORKFORCE)
06-11: myAlaska agentic AI autonomous multi-step government transactions (GOV IT)
06-10: RHTP transforms rural health with AI (RURAL TELEHEALTH)
06-09: data center 'just need an anchor tenant' gas-supply thesis (ENERGY/GAS)

candidate_claims.claim_verbatim: By making this land available, we are supporting the growing demands of the AI industry while generating value that directly supports our missions and the readiness of our Airmen and Guardians.
candidate_claims.claim_paraphrase_fair: The Department of the Air Force frames its Alaska AI data center leasing initiative as a defense-mission enabler that directly supports military readiness, not merely a real-estate or revenue play.

asserters.name: Robert Moriarty
asserters.title_or_org: Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Air Force for Installations

asserters.name: DAF press release (mirrored)
asserters.title_or_org: Department of the Air Force / Space Force news

candidate_claims.why_load_bearing: Defense contractors and capital allocators deciding whether to bid on the DAF Alaska AI data center leases (RLP deadline June 29, 2026) need to know whether the rationale is genuine defense-mission integration or real-estate monetization. If primarily revenue-driven, the mission-synergy premium is illusory and ROI/teaming assumptions change.

prelim_counter_evidence.fact: The DAF's Request for Lease Proposal requires operators to demonstrate how they will minimize and mitigate impacts to the surrounding community on energy, water, and bandwidth, and states the DAF receives at least fair market value in cash, signaling a revenue/real-estate model rather than mission-integration criteria.
ACEP/UAF analysis: Alaska's commercial electricity rates are much higher than any other US state, complicating the economic rationale that defense-mission framing does not address.

candidate_claims.recurrence_note: The 'directly supports our missions' framing is in the DAF release (Apr 10 2026) and repeated without scrutiny by Air & Space Forces Magazine, ClearanceJobs, Aviation A2Z, and Alaska's News Source (Apr-Jun 2026). Note: distinct from the already-corrected cooling/PUE angle and from the 06-15 satellite/sensor defense correction.
candidate_claims.orchestrator_note: TOP PICK. Fresh terrain (defense procurement real-estate-vs-mission), named senior official, primary counter-evidence in the lease terms themselves, live deadline June 29 2026. Desk-of-the-program-manager voice.

candidate_claims.claim_verbatim: the department's total potential value of contracts rose an astounding 1,605% to $90.7 billion from 2024, which represents 98.9% of the federal AI spend
candidate_claims.claim_paraphrase_fair: Federal AI contracting is so DoD-dominated (98.9% of total federal AI spend) that non-DoD agencies and the small/minority-owned firms they support receive negligible AI contract value, implying Alaska firms are largely locked out.

asserters.name: James S. Denford, Gregory S. Dawson, Kevin C. Desouza

candidate_claims.why_load_bearing: Alaska Native Corporations and Alaska-based federal contractors set business-development strategy on where federal AI dollars flow. If 98.9% is DoD-concentrated among large primes, ANC/small-business strategies anchored to civilian-agency AI work are structurally disadvantaged, especially with the 8(a) program under review through mid-2026.

prelim_counter_evidence.fact: Brookings itself notes small businesses captured 35% of all federal AI contracts by count (not value), with fastest growth at Treasury (+194%), DHS (+136%), VA (+81%) — agencies with Alaska-relevant missions. The count-vs-value distinction is material.

Alaska Native Corporations received over $11 billion in federal contracts in FY2021, more than half through the 8(a) sole-source pathway, which lets ANC subsidiaries compete for DoD contracts regardless of size — so DoD concentration is not necessarily inaccessible to AK entities (pathway under review as of Jan 2026).

candidate_claims.recurrence_note: Brookings data point picked up in federal-contracting commentary; ANC 8(a) story runs through KNBA, Alaska Public, ADN (Jan-Jun 2026). The Alaska-specific lockout implication requires a connecting inference the Brookings authors do not make.
candidate_claims.orchestrator_note: Fresh ANC/8(a) terrain. Risk: the 'Alaska firms locked out' framing is partly an inference rather than a directly asserted claim about Alaska. Validator should test attribution carefully.

candidate_claims.claim_verbatim: Our partnership with Saige introduces advanced AI capabilities to our state government functions, accelerating Alaska's IT modernization and ensuring that all residents benefit from cutting-edge technology and an improved digital experience.
candidate_claims.claim_paraphrase_fair: Alaska's Deputy Revenue Commissioner asserts the AI-enabled PFD application overhaul will accelerate state IT modernization and deliver cutting-edge benefits to all residents, with the contractor projecting 7 million minutes saved annually.

asserters.name: Fadil Limani
asserters.title_or_org: Deputy Commissioner, Alaska Department of Revenue

candidate_claims.why_load_bearing: The PFD touches 630,000+ applicants annually. The '7 million minutes saved' / 'millions in savings' claims are used to justify the procurement and benchmark state AI ROI. If AI components still require human analyst review of every application (contractor's own words), the automation/time-savings claims are overstated for procurement and oversight.

prelim_counter_evidence.fact: Charles Hu, the contractor projecting the savings, stated in the same announcement that 'while the system will utilize process automation, none of the systems are running automatically, and an analyst will still need to ensure that all application information is correct.'

Target go-live for a 'fully operational' system was early 2026 per the Dec 2024 announcement; as of June 2026 no state announcement of full operational status located, and the 2026 PFD cycle proceeded under existing processes.

candidate_claims.recurrence_note: Covered by StateScoop, GovTech, Route Fifty, Alaska Business, Alaska's News Source, GlobeNewswire. '7 million minutes' repeated verbatim without the contractor's qualification.
candidate_claims.orchestrator_note: Strong primary self-contradiction (contractor qualifies own claim). ADJACENCY RISK: the 06-11 correction was myAlaska agentic AI; this is the Saige PFD partnership ROI claim — a distinct claim/asserter but same PFD/state-IT terrain. Counter-evidence is mostly secondary (govtech outlets), not primary docket. Date is Dec 2024 (older).

candidate_claims.claim_verbatim: It positions Alaska to be highly competitive for federal AI education grants and other funding opportunities by demonstrating a clear, unified-level strategy
candidate_claims.claim_paraphrase_fair: DEED's computer science specialist asserts that publishing Alaska's K-12 AI framework makes the state highly competitive for federal AI education grants by demonstrating a unified state-level strategy.

asserters.name: Anthony White
asserters.title_or_org: Computer Science Content Specialist, Alaska Dept. of Education and Early Development (DEED)

candidate_claims.why_load_bearing: District technology-purchasing and grant-writing decisions are being calibrated on the premise that Alaska's framework creates a federal funding advantage. If Alaska was the 32nd state to issue guidance and the leading grant vehicle is unenacted, staff time and budget pointed at grant pursuits may be misallocated.

prelim_counter_evidence.fact: Alaska was the 32nd US state to issue K-12 AI guidance as of October 2025, meaning 31 states already had frameworks.

The NSF AI Education Act of 2026 (S.3957, 119th Congress), the leading federal AI-education grant vehicle, has not been enacted as of June 2026, so the grant programs referenced may not yet exist in funded form.

candidate_claims.recurrence_note: Framework release covered by Alaska Public/KTOO, MeriTalk State & Local, EdTech Innovation Hub, Ballotpedia, Alaska's News Source; 'highly competitive' claim reproduced in at least three.
candidate_claims.orchestrator_note: Fresh education/workforce terrain. Counter is partly primary (Congress.gov bill status). Risk: thinner AK business consequence (school districts, not capital/procurement at scale).

candidate_claims.claim_verbatim: Artificial Intelligence has the potential to help the Department of Energy and our National Labs accomplish enormous challenges in the fields of science and technology, as well as offer capabilities to streamline permitting for large-scale energy and critical mineral projects in Alaska.
candidate_claims.claim_paraphrase_fair: Sen. Murkowski asserts that AI deployed through DOE national labs can materially accelerate federal permitting for Alaska energy and critical-mineral projects.

asserters.name: Lisa Murkowski
asserters.title_or_org: U.S. Senator, Alaska (Chair, Senate ENR Committee)

candidate_claims.why_load_bearing: Alaska has billions in critical-mineral projects (Graphite Creek, Nikolai nickel) stuck in multi-year federal permitting queues. If AI-enabled permitting is the legislative solution being sold to industry and capital allocators, whether DOE AI can actually compress NEPA timelines is material for project finance.

prelim_counter_evidence.fact: The DOE AI Act was introduced July 2024 and has not been enacted; the Graphite Creek FAST-41 coverage was granted under existing authority, not the proposed AI Act.
CRS analysis of FY2026 NDAA AI provisions (IF13197) covers DoD AI security but contains no provision directing DOE to use AI to streamline Alaska mineral/energy permitting.

candidate_claims.recurrence_note: Circulates through Murkowski's official channels and Senate Energy Committee release; FedScoop and E&E covered the bill. Still a live talking point in AK critical-minerals investment conversations though unenacted.
candidate_claims.orchestrator_note: Fresh permitting/mining terrain, strong primary counter (CRS, Permitting Council). Risk: asserter quote is from July 2024 (older); is the steelman 'AI has the potential to streamline permitting' simply hedged/true-as-stated ('has the potential')? Validator must judge whether it survives the steelman test.

candidate_claims.claim_verbatim: We're proud to partner with Alaska Communications to help organizations across Alaska adopt AI confidently, securely and at scale.
candidate_claims.claim_paraphrase_fair: SurePath AI's CEO claims that, through the Alaska Communications partnership, organizations across Alaska can now adopt generative AI securely and at enterprise scale.
candidate_claims.why_load_bearing: The claim that AK businesses now have a secure at-scale GenAI onramp shapes mid-market enterprise and public-sector procurement decisions. If 'at scale' masks rural connectivity gaps, buyers may misjudge what is deployable.

prelim_counter_evidence.fact: FCC Broadband Data Collection maps show large portions of rural Alaska without fixed broadband at 25/3 Mbps; enterprise GenAI governance typically requires reliable high-bandwidth cloud connectivity not universally available.
GCI's Quintillion acquisition (Apr 2026) was framed as needed to extend fiber reach in underserved Arctic/rural communities, implying current coverage gaps persist.

candidate_claims.recurrence_note: Press release picked up verbatim by Yahoo Finance, Nasdaq, Barchart, Fiber Broadband Assoc, AI Journal, StockTitan on 2026-02-17 (one announcement, many pickups = ONE assertion).
candidate_claims.orchestrator_note: ADJACENCY RISK to 06-13 broadband correction (counter rests on connectivity gaps). Circulation is one press release syndicated, not independent assertions. Likely weaker on the circulation gate.

candidate_claims.claim_verbatim: Those who don't adopt AI will be left behind. For us, it's about using it to enhance how we work and protect our people while we do it.
candidate_claims.claim_paraphrase_fair: Silver Bay Seafoods' IT Director asserts that AI adoption is a survival imperative for Alaska seafood processors.

asserters.name: Martin Wagner
asserters.title_or_org: Director of IT, Silver Bay Seafoods

candidate_claims.why_load_bearing: Silver Bay is one of Alaska's largest processors (10 facilities); the 'left behind' framing influences equipment and training spend across the salmon/halibut industry.

prelim_counter_evidence.fact: The Alaska seafood industry posted losses over consecutive seasons; the Legislature debated a $60M aid package in May 2025, suggesting industry-wide financial distress is the primary competitive threat, not AI non-adoption.
Archipelago/ALFA AI electronic monitoring grant ($485K) noted AI video review is still in pilot for Alaska fisheries as of Aug 2025, indicating the industry is far from broad AI adoption.

candidate_claims.recurrence_note: Echoed in SeafoodSource and globalseafood.org but those are not Alaska-processor-specific. Wagner's case study is a 2024 vendor page.
candidate_claims.orchestrator_note: Fresh fisheries terrain but the claim is generic ('adopt or be left behind'), the source is an old vendor case study, counter-evidence is secondary. Weak on load-bearing and counter-quality.

candidate_claims.claim_verbatim: Alaska has done none of that. No comprehensive policy, no clear direction, no coordinated strategy.
candidate_claims.claim_paraphrase_fair: Alaska has produced no meaningful AI policy framework, strategic direction, or coordinated state-level approach to AI and data center development.

asserters.name: Anchorage Daily News Editorial Board
asserters.title_or_org: ADN Editorial Board (Ryan Binkley, Publisher; Gary Black, Opinion Editor)

candidate_claims.why_load_bearing: The 'Alaska has no AI strategy' framing shapes how legislators, investors, and federal agencies assess Alaska as a partner. If overstated, it could suppress investment or unfairly dismiss real legislative activity already in motion.

prelim_counter_evidence.fact: Alaska HB 47 (first AI-specific bill) passed the House 39-0 on Feb 27, 2026; HCR 3 established a Joint Legislative Task Force on AI; HB 259 (Rep. Mears) would set utility rate-setting guidelines for data centers.

The Alaska Center published a 'Data Centers on Our Terms' policy whitepaper in Jan 2026; DEED issued a K-12 AI Strategic Framework in Oct 2025 — both policy-shaping activity predating the April 2026 editorial.

candidate_claims.recurrence_note: 'No AI strategy' framing recurs in Stan Jones (Apr 12 2026 ADN), Roger Kaye (Feb 2026 ADN), and the RecordingLaw 'no comprehensive AI law' characterization. Two independent assertions (ADN board + RecordingLaw).
candidate_claims.orchestrator_note: Fresh governance/strategy angle with strong primary counter (HB 47 roll call, HCR 3, whitepaper). ADJACENCY: 06-11 was myAlaska agentic governance, but THIS is the policy-strategy-gap claim (distinct). Steelman survives: Alaska genuinely lacks a single coordinated economic-development AI strategy even though scattered bills exist — the correction is 'overstated, not none.' Solid #2 alternative to the DAF claim.

candidate_claims.claim_verbatim: Right now, it's about 12 milliseconds from Alaska to the coast of Oregon.
candidate_claims.claim_paraphrase_fair: Gov. Dunleavy asserts Alaska's fiber latency to the continental US is competitively low, making the state viable for latency-sensitive AI inference workloads.
candidate_claims.why_load_bearing: Dunleavy is pitching hyperscalers on Alaska for AI workloads; the latency claim is his core technical argument that AK can serve real-time inference, not just training/cold storage. If misleading, site-selection and incentive decisions rest on a faulty premise.

prelim_counter_evidence.fact: The 12ms figure is one-way terrestrial latency to Oregon; round-trip (24ms+) plus hops to major US cloud inference regions typically add 60-100ms total, above the sub-20ms threshold for low-latency inference APIs. The round-trip/end-to-end figure is not disclosed in the pitch.

GCI's Quintillion acquisition (Apr 2026) is framed as needed to add 1,800+ miles of Arctic fiber and reduce routing dependencies, implying current fiber architecture has gaps undercutting the latency pitch for non-Southcentral locations.

candidate_claims.recurrence_note: Latency pitch recurred at ASEC (Jun 2025), in pitch letters to Amazon/Meta/Microsoft, and in DCD/Alaska Current/KTOO coverage. DigitalBridge's Severin White endorsed it.
candidate_claims.orchestrator_note: Fresh data-center ANGLE (latency, not cooling/gas). Risk: Dunleavy has been the asserter in 4 of the last 6 corrections (asserter-fatigue), and the strongest counter is analytical/secondary. Technically defensible but tonally repetitive for the column.
